issues.failure_explanation: Writing m for the maximum update, m/(epsilon+m) is zero only when m is exactly zero and is close to one only when m greatly exceeds epsilon. For m=epsilon it equals 1/2, and for m much smaller than epsilon it is approximately m/epsilon. Consequently, with fixed positive epsilon and smooth updates m=O(h), the normalized coefficient does satisfy s=O(h^p). Normalization also cannot make nonzero floating-point updates exactly zero, unlike what the machine-precision and unnormalized-indicator comparison claims suggest.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof treats pre-merging followed by a merged-mesh FV update and blending. Under the printed full-mesh CFL the latter is not TVD: take alpha=0.2, a Delta t/h=0.5, upstream and left-cell values 1, and small-cell/downstream values 0. The raw pair becomes (1,2.5), its conservative mean is 1.25, and every blend leaves the small-cell value at least 1.25, increasing variation. The separate standing cellwise CFL would exclude this example, but would also impose the small-cell timestep restriction.

issues.failure_explanation: For fixed positive tau, large updates only approach s_infinity=1/(1+tau^p)<1. The residual delta=1-s_infinity therefore does not decrease with alpha. For the defined two-cell conservative average, the large-update amplification matrix has a stiff eigenvalue -delta nu/alpha+O(1). With the default p=2, tau=0.1, nu=0.5 and alpha=0.001, that eigenvalue is approximately -4.94. Being numerically close to full SRD is thus insufficient for alpha-uniform stability.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: U^*_j = U^n_j - \frac{\nu}{\alpha}(U^n_j - U^n_{j-1}),
R_j(s_j) = (1 - s_j) I + s_j S_j,

issues.failure_explanation: Stability concerns amplification, not the absolute size of one increment. Around a constant state write U=c+kappa v. The sensor gives s=O(kappa^p), while (S-I)B(U)=O(kappa), so the redistribution correction is O(kappa^(p+1)). The derivative of the complete update at that steady state is therefore the original upwind operator B. Under inflow conditions its small-cell mode has multiplier 1-nu/alpha, whose magnitude exceeds one when nu/alpha>2. Arbitrarily small perturbations can consequently be amplified even while redistribution is nearly off.

issues.failure_explanation: Even after correcting the averaging weights, the error is S epsilon+(S-I)u, not merely S epsilon. For weights A=1/(1+alpha) and B=alpha/(1+alpha), the left-cell formula needs B(u_j-u_left), and the small-cell formula needs A(u_left-u_j).
